Order: FeeClaimLib (CREATE2), ProveSettlement(stray,permit2), ProveExecutor, FeeDefaults+setDefaults+transferOwnership, ProveReader; then ProveBatchExecutor and RfqVenue with PROVE_SETTLEMENT_OFF_RECORD. FeeDefaults.acceptOwnership called from testnet admin 0x6fa7…6Acc (tx 0xd985e05d…). INTENT_TYPEHASH is now 0xc1e92b74… (fee-config model). Domain separator moved with the verifying contract. Old intents against 0xdb3843… are unspendable.
_relayer: Deployed by the settlement's own constructor, so the two bind immutably. It moved with this redeploy, which orphans every standing ERC-20 approval on the approval and permit rungs. A maker on the permit2 rung is unaffected: relayer.permit2() reads 0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3.
_verify: How to repeat the claim above: `cd contracts && node tools/verify-bytecode.mjs 943`. It reads this file, fetches eth_getCode for every address in `contracts`, and compares each one against the artifact forge build produced — reading the compiler's own immutableReferences rather than masking a guess, and printing each immutable's value with the record address it matches. Re-run on 2026-09-04 from a worktree at 9ff9265, the commit this record was written at: all eight matched instruction for instruction and every byte and nibble count above reproduced exactly. All eight metadata hashes differed, and that is a fact about the build rather than the program — solc hashes settings.remappings, and forge auto-detects those from whether lib/openzeppelin-contracts has its own submodules checked out and from the absolute path of the checkout. So the instruction bytes reproduce anywhere and the metadata hash reproduces only from an equivalent checkout at the same path. The tool exits 0 for identical, 3 for same program from a different build, and 1 for different code.
